item.title: The Birthday Paradox in Production: When Random IDs Collide
item.description:
You generate a UUID. It’s 128 bits total, with 122 bits of randomness ( Davis et al., 2024 ). That’s 340 undecillion possible values. Collision-proof, right? Your system generates a million IDs per second. Still safe? What about a billion?

As I like to say, common sense and intuition are the enemies of science. Common sense tells you that with 340,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 possible values, you’d need to generate at least trillions before worrying about duplicates. Maybe fill 1% of the space? 10%?
